newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ABN-AMRO Hungary unit offers health advice.
newsitem.headline: ABN-AMRO Hungary unit offers health advice.

text.p: ABN-AMRO Bank's Hungarian life insurance unit on Friday announced that it was offering access to a Dutch-owned tele-diagnosis service which allows users to seek a second medical opinion from U.S.-based physicians.

"We wanted to provide a new service to our clients and this worldwide novelty was well timed," Andras Farkas, Deputy General Director of ABN-AMRO Magyar Elet- es Nyugdijbiztosito Rt, told a news conference.
The move made Hungary the first country in central Europe with access to the tele-diagnosis franchise owned by Second Opinion International BV in the Netherlands.
The service has been available since January 1996 in the Netherlands, UK, Israel, Italy, Greece and France.
Farkas said a survey of more than 70,000 people showed that 90 percent were interested in the new product.
He said ABN-AMRO's Hungarian life and pension unit, launched in May, had some 1,000 clients and hoped to boost their numbers to between 30,000 and 40,000 by the end of the year.
Dutch banking group ABN-AMRO has been expanding in central and eastern Europe. Last year it bought an 89.23 percent stake in Magyar Hitel Bank and made a buyout offer for the rest of the shares.
On Thursday, ABN-AMRO chairman Jan Kalff said in Budapest the bank was considering buying more banks in eastern and central Europe.
